answer: Proof-of-Stake acts as a trellis for trust, requiring agents to commit collateral to validate state transitions. An attacker creating a hollow identity without capital incurs no financial penalty, but staking forces them to purchase native assets, creating a costly barrier to entry. As the network scales, each validator acts as a terrace of security, ensuring that increasing Sybil complexity requires a proportional rise in total staked capital, rendering massive fake-identity proliferation economically irrational.
